items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: My mother was named Rose. She was of the Barbarin family.

ctx.x: My mother was named Rose. She was of the Barbarin family. It was a huge family, Barbarins. My mother had, what?, four sisters and . . . four brothers and four sisters . . . four brothers and five sisters.
The Barbarin family is one of the most popular names in New Orleans music with names like Paul and Louis and Isidore. How is your mother related to them?

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: My mother's name was Ridley(?) Rose Barbarin, Paul Barbarin's sister.

ctx.x: Now, what was your mother's maiden name...?
Rose. My mother's name was Ridley(?) Rose Barbarin, Paul Barbarin's sister.

items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1959-06-30
items.q: since my father met my mother. He was Rose Barbera. He was a daughter of Isidot Barbera. A member of the original Longwood Brass Band.

ctx.x: Now where did you say he came from, Ball?

Ball came from Kentucky. Kentucky. It's a mystery to me how he came down south. He was going north. I think he was employed on one of the river boats. He settled in New Iberia. That's why I met my grandmother. He was born with four children. He moved in the Walther. And he worked as a stevedo, a long shaman on the river front. He read his children to tell the gun he came of age. He was not a twin, since my father met my mother. He was Rose Barbera. He was a daughter of Isidot Barbera. A member of the original…
